html:
SMTO-UI-0012 — This page doesn't know how to finish that command

GUID: 98341d37-45fd-4736-8e35-7a6d8cfc5c0e
Slug: ui-command-unavailable
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • You ran a command, but its last step is something this copy of the SMTO page can't do. That step wasn't carried out, though the command itself may already have run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Refresh the browser page. If SMTO was updated recently, close the tab and open SMTO again. This usually happens when the page you have open is older than the SMTO server it talks to.
  2. Open the same conversation and check whether the command already took effect, for example whether the task stopped or the status changed. The server may have finished the command even though this page couldn't show the final step.
  3. If it didn't take effect, run the command again from the message box or the Command palette. After refreshing, the page knows how to finish the commands the current SMTO offers.

What success looks like

  • The command runs and its result appears without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the command you typed, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A command result returned a client_action type that has no handler in the current browser client, so the follow-up action was not performed.

What this means

  • A command's client_action type has no supported handler in the current UI. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • A command's client_action type has no supported handler in the current UI.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare advertised client action type and installed handler registry.

How to fix it

  • The client_action.type in the commands/execute response is missing from the handler map in command_actions.js (desktop) or mobile/lazy/commands.js (mobile). This usually means the loaded page scripts are older than the Server; reload the page to fetch current assets, confirm the command's current state, and rerun only a command the current client supports.
  • Refresh command controls and choose an action advertised for the current task state.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A current supported command resolves to an available handler for the intended task.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
